summary.text: Bob Wirch is a Wisconsin state senator for the 22nd Senate District and has been in the Senate since 1996.

paragraphs.text: Wirch was born in Kenosha, Wisconsin, on November 16, 1943, according to his official biography, and graduated from Mary D. Bradford High School and earned a B.A. from UW-Parkside in 1970.
The page says he is a former factory worker and liaison to JTPA programs and served in the Army Reserve from 1965 to 1971.
It says he was a Kenosha County supervisor from 1986 to 1994, was elected to the Assembly in 1992 and reelected in 1994, and has been elected to the Senate since 1996.
The page lists a leadership position as minority caucus chair in 2003.
